analysis:
Examined BASE MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift:519–1435 and the bounded patch. Existing media paths reserve memory, reject unsupported controls, propagate deadlines/cancellation, and release acquired resources. Text and ordinary vision submissions carry requestCacheScope/cacheEnabled; several specialized media paths disable reuse. MiMo cluster caching at BASE:1389 is pre-existing, not a supported regression. These behaviors are relevant to A-001, A-018, T-010, T-028 and T-041; no supplied change establishes an authorization, encryption, billing or cache-isolation regression.
The patch adds GenerationLoopExitThinkingPolicy resolution at HEAD:1024–1029, excludes logprobs and distributed-pair serving, passes exitThinking into GenerationLoopGuardPolicy, and factors the existing stop-string scope into a local value. However, both primary units contain BASE source only. The patch stops before the substantial changed HEAD:1108–1169 stream handling, so its security effects cannot be verified here. Integration must examine the complete HEAD stream logic together with GenerationLoopExitThinkingPolicy, GenerationLoopGuardPolicy and bridge loop handling: verify injected thought-ending tokens cannot bypass answer/tool constraints, cause plaintext or cross-request disclosure, corrupt usage/cache identities, or leave generation running after cancellation. Check preservation of first-content deadlines and reservation release. No finding qualifies on the supplied evidence; uncertainty about the changed output transformation remains material.
